dantranh visible mic=5 prep=5 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness bend_range sustain mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch pillow spread_keys distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key knock sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation paper_buzz
flemish body 0
flemish label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
flemish label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
flemish label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
flemish label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
flemish label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
flemish label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
flemish label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
flemish label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
flemish label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
flemish label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
flemish label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
flemish label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
flemish label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
flemish label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
flemish label hammer_hardness Quill brightness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
flemish label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
flemish label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
flemish label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
flemish label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
flemish label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
flemish label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
flemish label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
flemish label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
flemish label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
flemish label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
flemish label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
flemish label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
flemish label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
flemish label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
flemish label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
flemish label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
flemish label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
flemish label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
flemish label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
flemish label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
flemish label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
flemish label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
flemish label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
flemish label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
flemish label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
flemish label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
flemish label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
flemish label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
flemish label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
flemish label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
flemish label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
flemish label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
flemish label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
flemish label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
flemish label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
flemish label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
flemish label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
flemish label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
flemish label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
flemish label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
flemish label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
flemish label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
flemish label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
flemish label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
flemish label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
flemish label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
flemish label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
flemish label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
flemish label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
flemish label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
flemish label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
flemish label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
flemish label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
flemish label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
flemish label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
flemish label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
flemish label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
flemish label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
flemish label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
flemish label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
flemish label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

flemish visible mic=5 prep=5 stop_8 stop_4 stop_8b lute buff sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness sustain mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch lid lid_off pillow distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key knock release sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_hammers wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation paper_buzz
french body 0
french label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
french label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
french label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
french label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
french label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
french label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
french label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
french label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
french label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
french label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
french label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
french label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
french label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
french label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
french label hammer_hardness Quill brightness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
french label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
french label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
french label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
french label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
french label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
french label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
french label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
french label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
french label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
french label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
french label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
french label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
french label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
french label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
french label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
french label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
french label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
french label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
french label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
french label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
french label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
french label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
french label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
french label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
french label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
french label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
french label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
french label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
french label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
french label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
french label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
french label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
french label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
french label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
french label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
french label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
french label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
french label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
french label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
french label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
french label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
french label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
french label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
french label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
french label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
french label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
french label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
french label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
french label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
french label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
french label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
french label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
french label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
french label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
french label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
french label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
french label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
french label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
french label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
french label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
french label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

glockenspiel body 7
glockenspiel label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
glockenspiel label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
glockenspiel label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
glockenspiel label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
glockenspiel label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
glockenspiel label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
glockenspiel label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
glockenspiel label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
glockenspiel label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
glockenspiel label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
glockenspiel label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
glockenspiel label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
glockenspiel label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
glockenspiel label hammer_hardness Mallet hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
glockenspiel label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
glockenspiel label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
glockenspiel label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
glockenspiel label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
glockenspiel label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
glockenspiel label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
glockenspiel label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
glockenspiel label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
glockenspiel label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
glockenspiel label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
glockenspiel label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
glockenspiel label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
glockenspiel label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
glockenspiel label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
glockenspiel label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
glockenspiel label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
glockenspiel label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
glockenspiel label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
glockenspiel label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
glockenspiel label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
glockenspiel label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
glockenspiel label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
glockenspiel label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
glockenspiel label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
glockenspiel label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
glockenspiel label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
glockenspiel label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
glockenspiel label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
glockenspiel label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
glockenspiel label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
glockenspiel label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
glockenspiel label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
glockenspiel label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
glockenspiel label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
glockenspiel label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
glockenspiel label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
glockenspiel label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
glockenspiel label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
glockenspiel label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
glockenspiel label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
glockenspiel label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
glockenspiel label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
glockenspiel label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
glockenspiel label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
glockenspiel label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
glockenspiel label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
glockenspiel label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
glockenspiel label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
glockenspiel label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
glockenspiel label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
glockenspiel label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
glockenspiel label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
glockenspiel label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

glockenspiel_b body 7
glockenspiel_b label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
glockenspiel_b label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
glockenspiel_b label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
glockenspiel_b label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel_b label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
glockenspiel_b label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
glockenspiel_b label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
glockenspiel_b label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
glockenspiel_b label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
glockenspiel_b label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
glockenspiel_b label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
glockenspiel_b label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
glockenspiel_b label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
glockenspiel_b label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
glockenspiel_b label hammer_hardness Mallet hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
glockenspiel_b label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
glockenspiel_b label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
glockenspiel_b label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
glockenspiel_b label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
glockenspiel_b label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
glockenspiel_b label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
glockenspiel_b label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
glockenspiel_b label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
glockenspiel_b label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
glockenspiel_b label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
glockenspiel_b label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
glockenspiel_b label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
glockenspiel_b label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
glockenspiel_b label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
glockenspiel_b label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
glockenspiel_b label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
glockenspiel_b label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
glockenspiel_b label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
glockenspiel_b label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
glockenspiel_b label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
glockenspiel_b label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
glockenspiel_b label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
glockenspiel_b label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
glockenspiel_b label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
glockenspiel_b label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
glockenspiel_b label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
glockenspiel_b label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
glockenspiel_b label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
glockenspiel_b label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
glockenspiel_b label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
glockenspiel_b label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
glockenspiel_b label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
glockenspiel_b label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
glockenspiel_b label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
glockenspiel_b label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
glockenspiel_b label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
glockenspiel_b label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
glockenspiel_b label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
glockenspiel_b label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
glockenspiel_b label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
glockenspiel_b label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
glockenspiel_b label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
glockenspiel_b label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
glockenspiel_b label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel_b label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
glockenspiel_b label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
glockenspiel_b label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
glockenspiel_b label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
glockenspiel_b label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel_b label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
glockenspiel_b label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
glockenspiel_b label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
glockenspiel_b label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
glockenspiel_b label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel_b label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
glockenspiel_b label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel_b label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel_b label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel_b label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel_b label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
glockenspiel_b label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

grand_a label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
grand_a label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
grand_a label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
grand_a label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
grand_a label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
grand_a label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
grand_a label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
grand_a label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
grand_a label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
grand_a label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
grand_a label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
grand_a label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
grand_a label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
grand_a label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
grand_a label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
grand_a label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
grand_a label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_a label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
grand_a label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
grand_a label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
grand_a label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
grand_a label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_a label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
grand_a label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
grand_a label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
grand_a label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
grand_a label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
grand_a label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
grand_a label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
grand_a label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
grand_a label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_a label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
grand_a label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
grand_a label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
grand_a label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
grand_a label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_a label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
grand_a label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
grand_a label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
grand_a label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
grand_a label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_a label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
grand_a label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_a label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_a label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_a label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_a label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_a label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

grand_b body 0
grand_b label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
grand_b label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
grand_b label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
grand_b label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_b label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
grand_b label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
grand_b label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
grand_b label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
grand_b label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
grand_b label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_b label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
grand_b label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
grand_b label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
grand_b label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_b label hammer_hardness Hammer hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
grand_b label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
grand_b label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
grand_b label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
grand_b label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
grand_b label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
grand_b label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
grand_b label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
grand_b label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
grand_b label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
grand_b label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
grand_b label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
grand_b label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
grand_b label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
grand_b label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
grand_b label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
grand_b label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
grand_b label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
grand_b label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
grand_b label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
grand_b label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
grand_b label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
grand_b label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
grand_b label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
grand_b label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
grand_b label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
grand_b label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
grand_b label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
grand_b label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
grand_b label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
grand_b label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_b label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
grand_b label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
grand_b label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
grand_b label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
grand_b label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_b label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
grand_b label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
grand_b label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
grand_b label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
grand_b label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
grand_b label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
grand_b label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
grand_b label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
grand_b label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_b label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
grand_b label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
grand_b label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
grand_b label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
grand_b label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_b label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
grand_b label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
grand_b label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
grand_b label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
grand_b label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_b label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
grand_b label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_b label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_b label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_b label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_b label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_b label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.
