grand_g visible mic=5 prep=4 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness dynamics sustain board_bass variation restrike mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch lid lid_off pillow distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key stretch unison_width knock release pedal_noise sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_hammers wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_unisons wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard hammer_grooves damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation bolt_mass bolt_position
grand_g visible mic=5 prep=5 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness dynamics sustain board_bass variation restrike mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch lid lid_off pillow distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key stretch unison_width knock release pedal_noise sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_hammers wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_unisons wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard hammer_grooves damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation paper_buzz
grand_h body 0
grand_h label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
grand_h label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
grand_h label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
grand_h label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_h label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
grand_h label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
grand_h label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
grand_h label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
grand_h label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
grand_h label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_h label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
grand_h label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
grand_h label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
grand_h label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_h label hammer_hardness Hammer hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
grand_h label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
grand_h label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
grand_h label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
grand_h label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
grand_h label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
grand_h label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
grand_h label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
grand_h label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
grand_h label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
grand_h label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
grand_h label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
grand_h label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
grand_h label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
grand_h label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
grand_h label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
grand_h label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
grand_h label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
grand_h label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
grand_h label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
grand_h label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
grand_h label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
grand_h label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
grand_h label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
grand_h label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
grand_h label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
grand_h label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
grand_h label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
grand_h label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
grand_h label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
grand_h label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_h label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
grand_h label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
grand_h label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
grand_h label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
grand_h label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_h label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
grand_h label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
grand_h label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
grand_h label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
grand_h label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
grand_h label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
grand_h label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
grand_h label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
grand_h label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_h label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
grand_h label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
grand_h label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
grand_h label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
grand_h label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_h label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
grand_h label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
grand_h label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
grand_h label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
grand_h label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_h label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
grand_h label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_h label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_h label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_h label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_h label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_h label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

grand_h visible mic=5 prep=4 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness dynamics sustain board_bass variation restrike mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch lid lid_off pillow distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key stretch unison_width knock release pedal_noise sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_hammers wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_unisons wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard hammer_grooves damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation bolt_mass bolt_position
grand_h visible mic=5 prep=5 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness dynamics sustain board_bass variation restrike mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch lid lid_off pillow distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key stretch unison_width knock release pedal_noise sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_hammers wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_unisons wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard hammer_grooves damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation paper_buzz
grand_i body 0
grand_i label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
grand_i label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
grand_i label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
grand_i label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_i label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
grand_i label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
grand_i label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
grand_i label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
grand_i label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
grand_i label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_i label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
grand_i label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
grand_i label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
grand_i label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_i label hammer_hardness Hammer hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
grand_i label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
grand_i label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
grand_i label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
grand_i label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
grand_i label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
grand_i label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
grand_i label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
grand_i label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
grand_i label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
grand_i label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
grand_i label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
grand_i label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
grand_i label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
grand_i label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
grand_i label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
grand_i label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
grand_i label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
grand_i label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
grand_i label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
grand_i label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
grand_i label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
grand_i label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
grand_i label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
grand_i label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
grand_i label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
grand_i label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
grand_i label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
grand_i label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
grand_i label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
grand_i label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_i label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
grand_i label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
grand_i label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
grand_i label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
grand_i label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
grand_i label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
grand_i label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
grand_i label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
grand_i label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
grand_i label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
grand_i label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
grand_i label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
grand_i label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
grand_i label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_i label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
grand_i label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
grand_i label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
grand_i label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
grand_i label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_i label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
grand_i label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
grand_i label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
grand_i label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
grand_i label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_i label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
grand_i label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_i label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_i label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_i label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_i label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
grand_i label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

guitar body 9
guitar label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
guitar label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
guitar label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
guitar label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
guitar label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
guitar label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
guitar label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
guitar label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
guitar label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
guitar label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
guitar label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
guitar label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
guitar label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
guitar label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
guitar label hammer_hardness Finger brightness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
guitar label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
guitar label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
guitar label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
guitar label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
guitar label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
guitar label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
guitar label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
guitar label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
guitar label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
guitar label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
guitar label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
guitar label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
guitar label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
guitar label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
guitar label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
guitar label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
guitar label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
guitar label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
guitar label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
guitar label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
guitar label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
guitar label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
guitar label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
guitar label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
guitar label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
guitar label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
guitar label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
guitar label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
guitar label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
guitar label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
guitar label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
guitar label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
guitar label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
guitar label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
guitar label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
guitar label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
guitar label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
guitar label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
guitar label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
guitar label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
guitar label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
guitar label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
guitar label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
guitar label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
guitar label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
guitar label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
guitar label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
guitar label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
guitar label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
guitar label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
guitar label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
guitar label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
guitar label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
guitar label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
guitar label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
guitar label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
guitar label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
guitar label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
guitar label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
guitar label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
guitar label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

handchimes body 11
handchimes label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
handchimes label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
handchimes label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
handchimes label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
handchimes label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
handchimes label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
handchimes label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
handchimes label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
handchimes label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
handchimes label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
handchimes label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
handchimes label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
handchimes label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
handchimes label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
handchimes label hammer_hardness Mallet hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
handchimes label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
handchimes label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
handchimes label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
handchimes label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
handchimes label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
handchimes label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
handchimes label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
handchimes label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
handchimes label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
handchimes label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
handchimes label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
handchimes label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
handchimes label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
handchimes label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
handchimes label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
handchimes label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
handchimes label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
handchimes label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
handchimes label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
handchimes label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
handchimes label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
handchimes label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
handchimes label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
handchimes label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
handchimes label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
handchimes label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
handchimes label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
handchimes label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
handchimes label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
handchimes label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
handchimes label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
handchimes label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
handchimes label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
handchimes label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
handchimes label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
handchimes label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
handchimes label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
handchimes label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
handchimes label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
handchimes label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
handchimes label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
handchimes label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
handchimes label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
handchimes label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
handchimes label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
handchimes label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
handchimes label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
handchimes label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
handchimes label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
handchimes label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
handchimes label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
handchimes label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
handchimes label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
handchimes label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
handchimes label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
handchimes label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
handchimes label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
handchimes label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
handchimes label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
handchimes label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
handchimes label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

harp body 2
harp label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
harp label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
harp label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
harp label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
harp label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
harp label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
harp label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
harp label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
harp label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
harp label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
harp label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
harp label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
harp label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
harp label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
harp label hammer_hardness Finger brightness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
harp label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
harp label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
harp label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
harp label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
harp label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
harp label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
harp label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
harp label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
harp label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
harp label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
harp label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
harp label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
harp label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
harp label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
harp label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
harp label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
harp label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
harp label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
harp label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
harp label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
harp label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
harp label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
harp label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
harp label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
harp label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
harp label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
harp label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
harp label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
harp label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
harp label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
harp label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
harp label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
harp label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
harp label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
harp label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
harp label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
harp label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
harp label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
harp label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
harp label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
harp label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
harp label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
harp label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
harp label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
harp label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
harp label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
harp label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
harp label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
harp label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
harp label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
harp label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
harp label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
harp label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
harp label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
harp label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
harp label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
harp label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
harp label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
harp label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
harp label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
harp label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.
