leverharp body 3
leverharp label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
leverharp label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
leverharp label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
leverharp label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
leverharp label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
leverharp label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
leverharp label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
leverharp label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
leverharp label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
leverharp label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
leverharp label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
leverharp label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
leverharp label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
leverharp label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
leverharp label hammer_hardness Finger brightness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
leverharp label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
leverharp label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
leverharp label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
leverharp label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
leverharp label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
leverharp label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
leverharp label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
leverharp label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
leverharp label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
leverharp label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
leverharp label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
leverharp label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
leverharp label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
leverharp label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
leverharp label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
leverharp label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
leverharp label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
leverharp label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
leverharp label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
leverharp label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
leverharp label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
leverharp label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
leverharp label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
leverharp label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
leverharp label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
leverharp label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
leverharp label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
leverharp label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
leverharp label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
leverharp label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
leverharp label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
leverharp label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
leverharp label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
leverharp label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
leverharp label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
leverharp label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
leverharp label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
leverharp label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
leverharp label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
leverharp label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
leverharp label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
leverharp label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
leverharp label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
leverharp label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
leverharp label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
leverharp label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
leverharp label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
leverharp label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
leverharp label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
leverharp label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
leverharp label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
leverharp label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
leverharp label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
leverharp label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
leverharp label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
leverharp label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
leverharp label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
leverharp label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
leverharp label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
leverharp label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
leverharp label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

marimba body 5
marimba label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
marimba label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
marimba label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
marimba label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
marimba label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
marimba label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
marimba label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
marimba label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
marimba label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
marimba label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
marimba label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
marimba label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
marimba label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
marimba label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
marimba label hammer_hardness Mallet hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
marimba label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
marimba label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
marimba label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
marimba label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
marimba label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
marimba label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
marimba label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
marimba label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
marimba label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
marimba label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
marimba label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
marimba label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
marimba label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
marimba label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
marimba label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
marimba label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
marimba label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
marimba label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
marimba label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
marimba label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
marimba label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
marimba label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
marimba label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
marimba label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
marimba label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
marimba label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
marimba label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
marimba label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
marimba label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
marimba label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
marimba label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
marimba label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
marimba label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
marimba label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
marimba label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
marimba label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
marimba label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
marimba label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
marimba label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
marimba label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
marimba label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
marimba label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
marimba label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
marimba label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
marimba label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
marimba label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
marimba label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
marimba label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
marimba label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
marimba label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
marimba label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
marimba label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
marimba label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
marimba label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
marimba label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
marimba label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
marimba label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
marimba label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
marimba label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
marimba label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
marimba label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

mavembe body 12
mavembe label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
mavembe label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
mavembe label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
mavembe label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
mavembe label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
mavembe label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
mavembe label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
mavembe label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
mavembe label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
mavembe label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
mavembe label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
mavembe label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
mavembe label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
mavembe label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
mavembe label hammer_hardness Thumb brightness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
mavembe label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
mavembe label knock Thumb click|The thumb's click on the tine at each note, against the recording. The left end is off.
mavembe label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
mavembe label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
mavembe label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
mavembe label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
mavembe label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
mavembe label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
mavembe label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
mavembe label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
mavembe label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
mavembe label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
mavembe label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
mavembe label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
mavembe label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
mavembe label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
mavembe label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
mavembe label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
mavembe label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
mavembe label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
mavembe label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
mavembe label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
mavembe label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
mavembe label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
mavembe label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
mavembe label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
mavembe label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
mavembe label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
mavembe label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
mavembe label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
mavembe label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
mavembe label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
mavembe label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
mavembe label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
mavembe label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
mavembe label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
mavembe label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
mavembe label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
mavembe label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
mavembe label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
mavembe label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
mavembe label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
mavembe label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
mavembe label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
mavembe label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
mavembe label sympathetic Ringing tines|How strongly the other tines ring along with the played one: 100 % as recorded (in the treble the bass tines outlast the played one), 0 off, more exaggerates it.
mavembe label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
mavembe label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
mavembe label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
mavembe label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
mavembe label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
mavembe label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
mavembe label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
mavembe label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
mavembe label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
mavembe label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
mavembe label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
mavembe label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
mavembe label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
mavembe label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
mavembe label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

mbira label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
mbira label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
mbira label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
mbira label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
mbira label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
mbira label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
mbira label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
mbira label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
mbira label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
mbira label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
mbira label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
mbira label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
mbira label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
mbira label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
mbira label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
mbira label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
mbira label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
mbira label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
mbira label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
mbira label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
mbira label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
mbira label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
mbira label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
mbira label sympathetic Ringing tines|How strongly the other tines ring along with the played one: 100 % as recorded (in the treble the bass tines outlast the played one), 0 off, more exaggerates it.
mbira label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
mbira label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
mbira label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
mbira label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
mbira label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
mbira label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
mbira label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
mbira label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
mbira label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
mbira label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
mbira label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
mbira label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
mbira label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
mbira label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
mbira label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

nyunga body 12
nyunga label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
nyunga label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
nyunga label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
nyunga label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
nyunga label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
nyunga label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
nyunga label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
nyunga label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
nyunga label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
nyunga label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
nyunga label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
nyunga label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
nyunga label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
nyunga label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
nyunga label hammer_hardness Thumb brightness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
nyunga label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
nyunga label knock Thumb click|The thumb's click on the tine at each note, against the recording. The left end is off.
nyunga label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
nyunga label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
nyunga label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
nyunga label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
nyunga label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
nyunga label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
nyunga label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
nyunga label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
nyunga label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
nyunga label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
nyunga label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
nyunga label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
nyunga label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
nyunga label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
nyunga label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
nyunga label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
nyunga label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
nyunga label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
nyunga label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
nyunga label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
nyunga label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
nyunga label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
nyunga label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
nyunga label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
nyunga label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
nyunga label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
nyunga label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
nyunga label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
nyunga label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
nyunga label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
nyunga label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
nyunga label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
nyunga label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
nyunga label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
nyunga label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
nyunga label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
nyunga label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
nyunga label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
nyunga label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
nyunga label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
nyunga label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
nyunga label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
nyunga label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
nyunga label sympathetic Ringing tines|How strongly the other tines ring along with the played one: 100 % as recorded (in the treble the bass tines outlast the played one), 0 off, more exaggerates it.
nyunga label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
nyunga label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
nyunga label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
nyunga label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
nyunga label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
nyunga label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
nyunga label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
nyunga label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
nyunga label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
nyunga label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
nyunga label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
nyunga label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
nyunga label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
nyunga label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
nyunga label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

psaltery body 14
psaltery label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
psaltery label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
psaltery label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
psaltery label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
psaltery label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
psaltery label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
psaltery label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
psaltery label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
psaltery label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
psaltery label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
psaltery label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
psaltery label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
psaltery label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
psaltery label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
psaltery label hammer_hardness Pick brightness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
psaltery label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
psaltery label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
psaltery label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
psaltery label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
psaltery label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
psaltery label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
psaltery label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
psaltery label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
psaltery label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
psaltery label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
psaltery label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
psaltery label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
psaltery label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
psaltery label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
psaltery label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
psaltery label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
psaltery label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
psaltery label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
psaltery label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
psaltery label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
psaltery label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
psaltery label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
psaltery label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
psaltery label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
psaltery label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
psaltery label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
psaltery label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
psaltery label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
psaltery label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
psaltery label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
psaltery label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
psaltery label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
psaltery label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
psaltery label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
psaltery label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
psaltery label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
psaltery label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
psaltery label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
psaltery label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
psaltery label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
psaltery label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
psaltery label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
psaltery label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
psaltery label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
psaltery label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
psaltery label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
psaltery label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
psaltery label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
psaltery label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
psaltery label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
psaltery label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
psaltery label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
psaltery label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
psaltery label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
psaltery label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
psaltery label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
psaltery label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
psaltery label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
psaltery label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
psaltery label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
psaltery label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.
