psaltery visible mic=5 prep=5 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness sustain mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch pillow spread_keys distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key knock sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation paper_buzz
strumstick body 16
strumstick label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
strumstick label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
strumstick label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
strumstick label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
strumstick label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
strumstick label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
strumstick label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
strumstick label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
strumstick label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
strumstick label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
strumstick label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
strumstick label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
strumstick label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
strumstick label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
strumstick label hammer_hardness Finger brightness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
strumstick label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
strumstick label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
strumstick label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
strumstick label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
strumstick label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
strumstick label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
strumstick label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
strumstick label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
strumstick label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
strumstick label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
strumstick label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
strumstick label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
strumstick label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
strumstick label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
strumstick label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
strumstick label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
strumstick label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
strumstick label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
strumstick label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
strumstick label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
strumstick label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
strumstick label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
strumstick label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
strumstick label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
strumstick label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
strumstick label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
strumstick label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
strumstick label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
strumstick label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
strumstick label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
strumstick label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
strumstick label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
strumstick label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
strumstick label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
strumstick label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
strumstick label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
strumstick label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
strumstick label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
strumstick label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
strumstick label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
strumstick label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
strumstick label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
strumstick label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
strumstick label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
strumstick label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
strumstick label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
strumstick label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
strumstick label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
strumstick label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
strumstick label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
strumstick label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
strumstick label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
strumstick label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
strumstick label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
strumstick label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
strumstick label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
strumstick label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
strumstick label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
strumstick label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
strumstick label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
strumstick label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

strumstick visible mic=5 prep=5 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness sustain mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch pillow spread_keys distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key knock sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation paper_buzz
upright_a body 1
upright_a label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
upright_a label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
upright_a label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
upright_a label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_a label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
upright_a label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
upright_a label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
upright_a label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
upright_a label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
upright_a label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_a label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
upright_a label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
upright_a label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
upright_a label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_a label hammer_hardness Hammer hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
upright_a label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
upright_a label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
upright_a label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
upright_a label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
upright_a label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
upright_a label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
upright_a label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
upright_a label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
upright_a label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
upright_a label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
upright_a label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
upright_a label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
upright_a label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
upright_a label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
upright_a label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
upright_a label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
upright_a label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
upright_a label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
upright_a label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
upright_a label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
upright_a label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
upright_a label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
upright_a label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
upright_a label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
upright_a label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
upright_a label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
upright_a label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
upright_a label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
upright_a label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
upright_a label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_a label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
upright_a label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
upright_a label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
upright_a label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
upright_a label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_a label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
upright_a label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
upright_a label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
upright_a label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
upright_a label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
upright_a label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
upright_a label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
upright_a label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
upright_a label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_a label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
upright_a label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
upright_a label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
upright_a label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
upright_a label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_a label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
upright_a label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
upright_a label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
upright_a label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
upright_a label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_a label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
upright_a label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_a label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_a label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_a label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_a label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_a label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

upright_a visible mic=5 prep=4 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness dynamics sustain board_bass variation restrike mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_wall mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch lid lid_off pillow distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key stretch unison_width knock release pedal_noise sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_hammers wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_unisons wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard hammer_grooves damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation bolt_mass bolt_position
upright_a visible mic=5 prep=5 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness dynamics sustain board_bass variation restrike mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_wall mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch lid lid_off pillow distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key stretch unison_width knock release pedal_noise sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_hammers wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_unisons wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard hammer_grooves damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation paper_buzz
upright_b body 1
upright_b label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
upright_b label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
upright_b label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
upright_b label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_b label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
upright_b label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
upright_b label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
upright_b label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
upright_b label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
upright_b label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_b label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
upright_b label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
upright_b label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
upright_b label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_b label hammer_hardness Hammer hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
upright_b label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
upright_b label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
upright_b label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
upright_b label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
upright_b label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
upright_b label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
upright_b label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
upright_b label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
upright_b label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
upright_b label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
upright_b label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
upright_b label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
upright_b label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
upright_b label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
upright_b label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
upright_b label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
upright_b label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
upright_b label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
upright_b label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
upright_b label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
upright_b label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
upright_b label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
upright_b label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
upright_b label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
upright_b label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
upright_b label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
upright_b label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
upright_b label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
upright_b label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
upright_b label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_b label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
upright_b label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
upright_b label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
upright_b label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
upright_b label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_b label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
upright_b label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
upright_b label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
upright_b label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
upright_b label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
upright_b label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
upright_b label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
upright_b label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
upright_b label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_b label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
upright_b label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
upright_b label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
upright_b label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
upright_b label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_b label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
upright_b label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
upright_b label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
upright_b label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
upright_b label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_b label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
upright_b label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_b label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_b label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_b label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_b label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_b label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

upright_b visible mic=5 prep=5 sustain_latch volume hammer_hardness dynamics sustain board_bass variation restrike mic_position mic_l_x mic_l_y mic_l_z mic_r_x mic_r_y mic_r_z mic_wall mic_l_pattern mic_l_yaw mic_l_pitch mic_r_pattern mic_r_yaw mic_r_pitch lid lid_off pillow distance_level room concert_pitch temperament temperament_key stretch unison_width knock release pedal_noise sympathetic audio_input damper_fall condition wear_variant wear_hammers wear_voicing wear_action wear_dampers wear_unisons wear_tuning wear_false_beats wear_strings wear_soundboard hammer_grooves damper_buzz rattle phantom preparation paper_buzz
upright_c body 1
upright_c label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
upright_c label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
upright_c label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
upright_c label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_c label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
upright_c label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
upright_c label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
upright_c label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
upright_c label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
upright_c label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_c label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
upright_c label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
upright_c label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
upright_c label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_c label hammer_hardness Hammer hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
upright_c label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
upright_c label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
upright_c label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
upright_c label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
upright_c label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
upright_c label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
upright_c label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
upright_c label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
upright_c label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
upright_c label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
upright_c label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
upright_c label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
upright_c label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
upright_c label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
upright_c label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
upright_c label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
upright_c label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
upright_c label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
upright_c label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
upright_c label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
upright_c label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
upright_c label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
upright_c label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
upright_c label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
upright_c label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
upright_c label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
upright_c label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
upright_c label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
upright_c label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
upright_c label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_c label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
upright_c label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
upright_c label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
upright_c label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
upright_c label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_c label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
upright_c label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
upright_c label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
upright_c label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
upright_c label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
upright_c label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
upright_c label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
upright_c label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
upright_c label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_c label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
upright_c label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
upright_c label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
upright_c label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
upright_c label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_c label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
upright_c label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
upright_c label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
upright_c label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
upright_c label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_c label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
upright_c label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_c label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_c label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_c label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_c label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_c label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

upright_d body 1
upright_d label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
upright_d label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
upright_d label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
upright_d label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_d label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
upright_d label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
upright_d label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
upright_d label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
upright_d label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
upright_d label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_d label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
upright_d label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
upright_d label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
upright_d label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_d label hammer_hardness Hammer hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
upright_d label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
upright_d label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
upright_d label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
upright_d label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
upright_d label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
upright_d label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
upright_d label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
upright_d label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
upright_d label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
upright_d label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
upright_d label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
upright_d label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
upright_d label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
upright_d label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
upright_d label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
upright_d label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
upright_d label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
upright_d label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
upright_d label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
upright_d label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
upright_d label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
upright_d label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
upright_d label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
upright_d label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
upright_d label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
upright_d label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
upright_d label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
upright_d label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
upright_d label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
upright_d label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_d label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
upright_d label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
upright_d label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
upright_d label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
upright_d label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
upright_d label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
upright_d label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
upright_d label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
upright_d label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
upright_d label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
upright_d label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
upright_d label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
upright_d label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
upright_d label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_d label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
upright_d label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
upright_d label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
upright_d label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
upright_d label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_d label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
upright_d label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
upright_d label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
upright_d label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
upright_d label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_d label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
upright_d label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_d label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_d label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_d label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_d label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
upright_d label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.
