vibraphone body 4
vibraphone label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
vibraphone label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
vibraphone label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
vibraphone label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
vibraphone label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
vibraphone label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
vibraphone label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
vibraphone label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
vibraphone label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
vibraphone label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
vibraphone label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
vibraphone label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
vibraphone label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
vibraphone label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
vibraphone label hammer_hardness Mallet hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
vibraphone label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
vibraphone label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
vibraphone label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
vibraphone label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
vibraphone label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
vibraphone label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
vibraphone label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
vibraphone label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
vibraphone label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
vibraphone label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
vibraphone label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
vibraphone label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
vibraphone label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
vibraphone label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
vibraphone label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
vibraphone label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
vibraphone label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
vibraphone label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
vibraphone label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
vibraphone label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
vibraphone label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
vibraphone label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
vibraphone label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
vibraphone label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
vibraphone label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
vibraphone label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
vibraphone label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
vibraphone label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
vibraphone label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
vibraphone label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
vibraphone label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
vibraphone label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
vibraphone label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
vibraphone label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
vibraphone label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
vibraphone label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
vibraphone label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
vibraphone label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
vibraphone label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
vibraphone label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
vibraphone label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
vibraphone label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
vibraphone label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
vibraphone label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
vibraphone label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
vibraphone label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
vibraphone label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
vibraphone label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
vibraphone label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
vibraphone label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
vibraphone label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
vibraphone label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
vibraphone label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
vibraphone label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
vibraphone label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
vibraphone label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
vibraphone label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
vibraphone label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
vibraphone label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
vibraphone label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
vibraphone label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.

xylophone body 6
xylophone label audio_input Audio input|Sound from the plugin's audio input reaches the strings: with the pedal down they ring along with it, as when singing into a grand; with it up only the strings without dampers do. The input itself is not played back. 0 dB drives the strings about as hard as their own sound at the same level. The left end is off. Beware of acoustic feedback with a microphone near the speakers.
xylophone label bebung Bebung|The clavichord's vibrato: a held key's pitch rises with the pressure on its tangent, by this much at full pressure. Played with the mod wheel, or with aftertouch (channel or per key; the highest counts). The clavichord
xylophone label bend_range Bend range|How far the pitch wheel bends the sounding notes, up or down: the left hand pressing the string behind its bridge. The dan tranh
xylophone label board_bass Bass|The strings' bass, as an equalizer on them: more or less of their sound below about 180 Hz, louder with it; the hammer's thud through the soundboard stays as it is. 0 is the instrument's own. Rebuilds the instrument.
xylophone label bolt_mass Bolt mass|A bolt or screw on every string: it bends the pitch and makes the overtones inharmonic.
xylophone label bolt_position Bolt position|Where along the strings the bolt sits: the partials with a node there are not affected.
xylophone label buff Buff|Pads on the strings for the next notes: shorter and darker (the harpsichords)
xylophone label concert_pitch Concert pitch|The pitch of A4. The strings are retuned: the instrument is rebuilt in the background and the sounding notes glide to the new tuning.
xylophone label condition Condition|The instrument's condition, in zones: Mint (0 %, as exported), Normal (to 10 %, the default: the keys a little uneven in loudness), Worn (to 35 %), Broken (to 100 %): harder hammers, worn dampers, a noisier action, drifting tuning and unisons, old strings and soundboard. The Condition tab shifts each aspect from here.
xylophone label damper_buzz Damper buzz|A damper that buzzes for a moment as it lands on the strings. 100 % is the most it should be.
xylophone label damper_fall Damper fall|How long a damper takes to land on the strings when a key is released, 100 % = about 25 ms at a normal release (faster for a fast release, slower for a slow one when the keyboard sends the release velocity). 0 = instant. A quick re-strike catches a damper in mid-fall.
xylophone label distance_level Distance level|Total: the level stays the same as you move away (far positions change little, the room dominates). Direct sound: the direct sound stays the same and the room grows with the distance; for an external reverb, set Room to Off.
xylophone label dynamics Dynamics|How much softer the softest key is than the hardest (the range from velocity 1 to 127): the loudest notes stay as recorded, less brings the soft ones up (struck harder, so also brighter), more takes them down. 45 dB as a recorded piano's sample set plays its layers. Pianos only.
xylophone label hammer_grooves Hammer grooves|Grooves the strings have worn into the hammer felt: a short, gritty noise at each strike, stronger when playing harder. 100 % is the most it should be.
xylophone label hammer_hardness Mallet hardness|How hard what strikes or plucks the string is (the hammer's felt, a mallet, a quill, a finger), from the next note: up brighter, down softer and rounder. 0 dB as recorded. On the pianos every key keeps its loudness: the felt is measured again in the background (a few seconds).
xylophone label harmonic Harmonic|The node a finger touches while the string is struck: 2 sounds the octave, 3 the twelfth, 4 the double octave, and so on.
xylophone label knock Action knock|The mechanism's noise at each note (a piano's key and hammer thump, a jack's knock), against the recording. The left end is off.
xylophone label lid Lid|How far the lid is open: 100 % is the full stick (grand) or the open top lid (upright), about 50 % a half stick, 0 % closed, which muffles the sound outside the case. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
xylophone label lid_off Lid removed|The lid taken off: nothing reflects the sound above the strings and nothing muffles it, as for a studio's microphones or an even sound in a small room; the Lid setting does nothing then. Needs a microphone position (the recording stands for the open lid).
xylophone label lute Lute|The lute row: the 8' II strings plucked near the nut, nasal, for the next notes (Harpsichord B)
xylophone label mic_distance Mic distance|0 = the position's default. Far positions (Audience) are mostly room: the distance changes little there.
xylophone label mic_l_pattern Left mic pattern|0 omni, 50 cardioid, 75 hypercardioid, 100 figure-8. A pattern hears what it points at; omni ignores the aim.
xylophone label mic_l_pitch Left mic tilt|Up or down from level, in degrees (positive: up). Omni ignores the aim.
xylophone label mic_l_x Left mic x|x across the piano (bass -, treble +), y along it (keyboard -, tail +), z up from the soundboard. Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets these.
xylophone label mic_l_y Left mic y|Left microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
xylophone label mic_l_yaw Left mic aim|Direction in the floor plane: 0 into the piano from the player's seat, positive towards the treble side.
xylophone label mic_l_z Left mic z|Left microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
xylophone label mic_position Mic position|Where the two microphones stand: Recording (the recording's own sound), Player (at the keyboard, the default), Audience (in front, at a distance), Close 1 and Close 2 (near the instrument, where the names say) or Custom (both placed freely). Click a marker in the drawing to choose one.
xylophone label mic_r_pattern Right mic pattern|As for the left microphone.
xylophone label mic_r_pitch Right mic tilt|As for the left microphone.
xylophone label mic_r_x Right mic x|Right microphone, x: across the piano (bass -, treble +). Dragging a microphone in the drawing sets x, y and z.
xylophone label mic_r_y Right mic y|Right microphone, y: along the piano (keyboard -, tail +).
xylophone label mic_r_yaw Right mic aim|As for the left microphone.
xylophone label mic_r_z Right mic z|Right microphone, z: the height above the soundboard.
xylophone label mic_spacing Mic spacing|How far apart the two microphones stand, across the line of sight: 0 is mono, more widens the stereo image. Dragging the pair in the drawing sets it.
xylophone label mic_wall Wall distance|Upright only: how far behind the board the wall stands.
xylophone label morph_x Morph X|Across the Morph tab's pad: with Morph Y, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph.
xylophone label morph_y Morph Y|Up the Morph tab's pad: with Morph X, the point whose distance to each corner sets that instrument's share of the morph. The top corner is the instrument chosen.
xylophone label motor Motor|The vibraphone's motor: discs in the resonators turn and the fundamentals swell and fade together (the vibraphone)
xylophone label motor_depth Motor depth|How far the fundamentals fade while the discs close the resonators: 100 % is about 12 dB (the vibraphone)
xylophone label motor_speed Motor speed|Pulses per second of the motor's tremolo (the vibraphone)
xylophone label mute Mute|How hard the hand rests on the strings while a key is down: 100 % is a dead thud. The highest notes have no dampers to rest on and are not muted.
xylophone label paper_buzz Paper buzz|Paper or a loose part on the strings: how much it buzzes with every note.
xylophone label pedal_noise Pedal noise|The sustain pedal's own noise: its thump going down and up, and the strings' ring when the dampers lift. The left end is off.
xylophone label phantom Phantom partials|More of the extra partials old, stiff strings make in loud bass notes (in full to C2, fading out by C3), beyond the instrument's own: a metallic, growling edge. 100 % is the most it should be.
xylophone label pillow Pillow|A pillow or blanket against the soundboard: the body sound gets duller, quieter and shorter.
xylophone label pluck_brightness Pluck brightness|How hard the finger or nail is: 100 % is a fingertip, more is a nail or a pick.
xylophone label pluck_position Pluck position|Where along the string it is plucked: near the end it is bright and thin, in the middle hollow.
xylophone label preparation Preparation|How the strings are prepared, the whole piano at once: plucked with a finger inside the piano, muted by a hand or felt, played as harmonics, with a bolt on the strings, or with buzzing paper.
xylophone label rattle Rattle|A loose part on the soundboard that rattles on loud low notes. 100 % is the most it should be.
xylophone label release Release noise|The noise when a key is let go (a damper landing, a jack falling back), against the recording. The left end is off.
xylophone label restrike Live re-strike|A note struck again while it still rings: the hammer meets the strings, the mallet the bar, where they are in their swing, so each repeat comes out a little different, harder where they swing towards it. Off: every strike as into still strings or a still bar. From the next note.
xylophone label room Room|The recording room's reverberation against the instrument's own sound. The left end is off: the dry instrument, for an external reverb.
xylophone label spread_keys Spread all keys|Bars, harps, guitars and zithers: all 88 keys spread along the instrument in front of the microphones (on, the default), or only its own range, with the keys beyond it sounding from its ends (off, as the real instrument)
xylophone label stop_4 Stop 4'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
xylophone label stop_8 Stop 8'|Register on or off, for the next notes (instruments with registers: Harpsichords B, E and F)
xylophone label stop_8b 8' II|The second 8' choir, for the next notes (Harpsichord B, derived; Harpsichords E and F, recorded); off while the lute plucks its strings
xylophone label stretch Stretch|Tuner's stretch on top of the recording's own tuning, computed from the strings' inharmonicity: bass flatter, treble sharper. 0 = as recorded, 1 adds a full tuner's stretch, -1 takes one off (pure octaves), more exaggerates it.
xylophone label sustain Sustain|How long the notes ring: 100 % as recorded, 200 % twice as long, 50 % half. Every partial decays that much slower or faster, its pitch and the attack kept. Not the sustain pedal. Rebuilds the instrument.
xylophone label sustain_latch Sustain latch|The sustain pedal held down while on (with MIDI CC64 and the on-screen pedal: the deepest counts): for MIDI files without pedal on the vibraphone and the harps, whose notes otherwise stop at the key's release
xylophone label sympathetic Sympathetic resonance|How strongly the undamped strings ring along with the played ones: 100 % as measured, 0 off, more exaggerates it. With the pedal down every string joins in.
xylophone label temperament Temperament|Equal (every key alike) or a historical temperament: keys near the temperament key sound purer, far ones more colorful. As recorded: each recorded key at its own pitch, as the instrument was tuned in the recordings. Scala file: a scale from a .scl file, any number of notes (a .kbm key map of the same name beside it lays it on the keys). A stays at the concert pitch.
xylophone label temperament_key Temperament key|The key a historical temperament or a Scala file's scale is centered on (its "C"). No effect with Equal temperament, As recorded or a Scala file with its own key map.
xylophone label unison_width Unison width|How far the strings of one note are detuned against each other: 100 % as recorded, 0 all alike (a steady tone), more a wider beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
xylophone label variation Strike variation|How much each strike differs from the last, as a real hammer never meets the strings quite the same way twice: the strike point, the moment and the felt per string. 100 % as measured on recorded takes, 0 every strike alike. From the next note.
xylophone label volume Volume|The output level, after everything else. The left end is off.
xylophone label wear_action Action noise|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a noisier action: louder knocks and releases.
xylophone label wear_dampers Dampers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): worn damper felt: notes ring on after the key is let go.
xylophone label wear_false_beats False beats|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): single strings beat by themselves, as uneven old strings do. Rebuilds the instrument.
xylophone label wear_hammers Hammers|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the felt compressed and harder: brighter, harsher strikes.
xylophone label wear_soundboard Soundboard|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): a tired soundboard: notes die away faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
xylophone label wear_strings Strings|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): old strings: overtones slightly off and dying faster. Rebuilds the instrument.
xylophone label wear_tuning Tuning|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the notes drift off pitch. Rebuilds the instrument.
xylophone label wear_unisons Unisons|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): the strings of a note drift apart: stronger beating. Rebuilds the instrument.
xylophone label wear_variant Variant|Another instrument of the same age: each variant draws other random deviations (which notes are out of tune, which hammers are worn). Rebuilds the instrument.
xylophone label wear_voicing Voicing|Shifts the overall Condition for this aspect (-100 % newer, +100 % older): hammers worn unevenly: neighboring notes differ in loudness and color.
